_note: Skeleton for docs/audit-rates-exemptions.json — the factory data file read by tests/test_audit_rates.py. Copy it into docs/ (the example itself is never read) and add an entry ONLY when a PUBLISHED close row's canonical run declares its `rework` disposition twice and NO LAWFUL PATH RESTORES IT. The row's run is read POSITIONALLY — the maximal trailing sequence of `=`-carrying tokens — so a prose token that carries `=` is absorbed into the run; where it collides with the trailer's own declaration, one disposition reads as two (the law gives a row ONE `rework` token). That collision EMPTIES the row's repair space at the instant it is written: `tools/ledger.py repair` composes `f"{head} {appended} {run}"`, inserting the appended text BEFORE the canonical run, so it cannot displace a token that lives INSIDE it, and the #104 re-declaration refusal blocks a second `rework=` — the one repair that would clear the leg is unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION. `bar` is a DECLARATION KEY WITH ONE LAWFUL VALUE on this surface, `repair-barred-by-construction`: the loader REQUIRES it and refuses every other value, so the wrong ground cannot be re-stated as data. NOTE THE SIBLING SURFACE DIFFERS, and the difference is the point (docs/instruments/ledger.md §9.12): docs/close-board-exemptions.json declares `no-truthful-value`, because ITS rows ARE reachable (its own recorded probe returns rc=0) and only the truthfulness of the value bars them. Reusing that value here would assert a reachability this row does not have, so it is REFUSED rather than discouraged. A claim of ABSENCE is a MECHANICAL claim, so an entry's `proof` must carry the RECORDED PROBE of the attempt — the command, its rc, and the effect read back (§9.3) — or the claim is not stated. Key every entry by the row's own `n` — the value the gate reads — so a FUTURE close (a different `n`) can never be excused by it. `reason` and `proof` are both REQUIRED, and `domain` must be the declared value 'the close row's canonical run declares its `rework` disposition twice'. It is printed as an 'excused:' line with its reason and proof on EVERY gate run IN BOTH INVOCATION MODES, so it is a visible debt rather than forgiveness, and the closing line distinguishes clean from excused. A malformed entry, or one that matches NO doubled row, is a gate ERROR rather than a silent pass. Expect this list to stay near-empty: one entry is a debt, and a SECOND is a process defect — the remedy for a second is a mechanism that stops the shape at the write path, never a third row. THAT MECHANISM NOW SHIPS: `tools/ledger.py append` REFUSES a detail whose canonical run declares the same key more than once, reading the run through the SHARED predicates (`trailer_tokens` and `token_key` in `tools/field_predicate.py`) so the refuser and the detector cannot drift. A second row of this shape therefore cannot be written at all; the entries in this file are history that no lawful repair reaches, and are the debt the mechanism retires. Nothing is ever backfilled: rewriting a published detail would be a falsified record, not a repair.
